title: This Is How You Solve the Housing Affordability Crisis
description:
Home ownership didn’t magically become impossible — it was engineered that way.

Runaway construction costs, foreign buyers gobbling up entire cities, institutional investors like BlackRock turning houses into rentals, illegal immigration driving up demand, and local governments inflating prices on purpose.

comments.text:
The median income in 1970, NOT adjusted for inflation (because this is how they lie to us), was $9,870
The median home price in 1970 was $23,000, so about 2.3 years worth of income (not including other bills, food etc!)
The median income now is $83,730
The median home price now is $415,000-$440,000, so about 5.25 years worth of income.

In the 1970s, a young man with a family and kids, working a blue collar job, could buy a home.
Now, you would have to make $166,000 per year to buy a home as comfortably as you would in 1970. 

The same has happened with cars, with about the same proportions.
